witness.evidence: Let f∈{0,1}, F=2f−1, and P(x)=Pr[output1] for an algorithm with failure probability at most e=1/3. Its expected-sign polynomial p=2P−1 satisfies ||p−F||∞≤2e=2/3 and has degree at most2T. For a unit-l1 dual measure μ annihilating all polynomials of degree<d, an exclusion argument requires <μ,F> > ||p−F||∞, thus correlation>2/3 for the direct conclusion Q_{1/3}≥d/2. Correlation merely>1/3 correctly certifies sign approximate degree at tolerance1/3; the exact LP results remain valid. Constant-error amplification can recover an Ω(d) query bound with a different constant, so this witness does not refute the asymptotic order merely because the threshold is1/3. It diagnoses the proposed unamplified direct interpretation, not any proved finite query-complexity value.
